芸.meaning: A street busker stands on a tuft of <part>grass</part> and flies a <part>kite</part> so precisely that it writes his name across the sky, then dives and snips one single blade from the lawn with its tail. The crowd throws coins. That's years of practised <kanji>technique</kanji>.
芸.on: Before every trick he taps a little pressure <sound>gau</sound>ge to check the wind.
芸.kun: Afterwards he plants the snipped blade back in the lawn and waters it with leftover <sound>u</sound>don broth: to plant.

視.meaning: A night-shift <part>lamppost</part> gets bored and borrows a tourist's <part>camera</part>. It zooms in on every passing dog, checking collars, paws and the shine on each nose, and jots notes in the dark. Every pup gets a full <kanji>inspection</kanji>.
視.on: A poodle that fails hides behind a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld until morning.
視.kun: 'Check <sound>me</sound> next!' yaps a puppy, sitting up straight under the light.

都.meaning: <part>Someone</part> in a hat sticks a <part>pennant</part> into a muddy field and whistles. Pop: a skyscraper shoots up. Another pennant, another tower, then trains, traffic and pigeons. By supper the field is a roaring <kanji>metropolis</kanji>.
都.on: Right in the middle stands a <sound>to</sound>tem pole taller than every skyscraper.
都.kun: 'Look at <sound>me</sound>!' shouts the mayor from the rail <sound>ya</sound>rd, waving a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala at the crowds.

際.meaning: Grandma keeps a <part>pennant</part> folded in a drawer and flies it for only one strange <part>ritual</part>: the day her tortoise finally wakes up from its winter sleep. Then the whole street dances round the shell in pyjamas. It's a rare <kanji>occasion</kanji>.
際.on: Everyone raises a mug of warm apple <sound>ci</sound>der to the yawning tortoise.
際.kun: A <sound>ki</sound>wi bird peeps out from the edge of the lawn: '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

並.meaning: A goat with little <part>horns</part> is in charge of a birthday party. It sets the <part>candles</part> on <part>one</part> long plank, then butts any that wobble out of place, until all hundred stand neatly side by side in a perfect <kanji>row</kanji>.
並.on: Then it munches the whole bale of <sound>hay</sound> it was given as a party present.
並.kun: The guests bring <sound>na</sound>an bread, every piece the same, nothing special: just average.

軽.meaning: A <part>tumbleweed</part> rolls across the desert and bumps into a parked <part>car</part>, and the car blows away with it, bouncing like a beach ball. It turns out to be made of paper. Off it drifts, skipping over the dunes <kanji>lightly</kanji>.
軽.on: Inside the paper car sits a birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke that floats up the moment the door opens.
軽.kun: One <sound>ca</sound>lm puff of wind lifts it again, along with a <sound>ru</sound>by ring left on the seat.

固.meaning: An <part>old</part> loaf of bread sits forgotten in a bird <part>cage</part> for a whole year. When the parrot finally pecks it, its beak bounces off with a clang. The baker uses it as a doorstop now: leave anything long enough and it will <kanji>harden</kanji>.
固.on: A <sound>ko</sound>ala borrows the loaf to crack nuts on.
固.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp tries to nibble it too, then gives up and eats a <sound>ta</sound>co instead.

密.meaning: High on a <part>mountain</part>, a hermit hides his diary in the <part>attic</part> of his hut, under nine locks and a sleeping bear. He never says a word about it, not even to his goats. His whole life runs on <kanji>secrecy</kanji>.
密.on: Once a year he <sound>meets</sound> the bear at midnight to swap new passwords.
密.kun: <sound>He</sound> keeps the very last key rolled up in an old <sound>so</sound>ck.

端.meaning: A wizard with a <part>beard</part> so long it trails behind him climbs a <part>mountain</part> and takes his <part>stand</part> on the very last rock, toes over nothing. The wind tugs his beard out over the drop like a flag. He's right on the <kanji>edge</kanji>.
端.on: Far below, a train roars out of a <sound>tun</sound>nel and toots at his dangling beard.
端.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' he laughs, and holds up a <sound>shi</sound>eld against the wind.

途.meaning: A delivery robot carries <part>too much</part>: twelve pizzas, a sofa and a goat. It can't fit through the door, so it rolls down a <part>ramp</part>, round the duck pond, under the bridge and through the car wash. That's its usual <kanji>route</kanji>.
途.on: It steers by the <sound>to</sound>tem pole in the town square, turning left every time.
途.kun: 'Feed <sound>me</sound> <sound>chee</sound>se!' bleats the goat on top at every corner.

労.meaning: A strongman who is all <part>muscle</part> spends the whole night hauling crates up a hill for the town's <part>fireworks</part>. When they finally bang, he's asleep under a <part>blanket</part> on the grass, too tired to look. Nobody sees his hard <kanji>labor</kanji>.
労.on: Someone tucks a red <sound>ro</sound>se into his sleeping hand to say thanks.
労.kun: '<sound>Ea</sound>t this <sound>ta</sound>co,' says his mum, hugging him. '<sound>Wah</sound>, you worked so hard!'

兵.meaning: A spider in a thimble helmet guards the top of a <part>hill</part>, marching back and forth on all <part>eight</part> legs with a toothpick over its shoulder. Left, right, left, right, left, right, left, right. It's the bravest little <kanji>soldier</kanji>.
兵.on: At night it sleeps in a bale of <sound>hay</sound> with its helmet still on.
兵.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' it sneezes. '<sound>Wah</sound>!' It grabs a <sound>mo</sound>p to fight, but it's <sound>no</sound>t an enemy, just dust.

派.meaning: A river reaches the sea and splits into a <part>river delta</part>, a dozen streams fanning out. Each stream of <part>water drops</part> insists it's the real river, gives itself a name and a flag, and won't talk to the others. Every branch is its own <kanji>faction</kanji>.
派.on: Each stream builds its own little <sound>hu</sound>t on its bank and argues from the doorway.

散.meaning: Under the <part>moon</part>, <part>two</part> kids play football with a dandelion clock beside the pool. One leaps off the <part>diving board</part> and kicks it at the <part>goal</part>, the other swipes at it with a paper <part>fan</part>, and whoosh: a thousand fluffy seeds blow across the water. Every one of them flies off to <kanji>scatter</kanji>.
散.on: One seed lands right on top of a chocolate <sound>sun</sound>dae.
散.kun: The rest settle on a block of <sound>chee</sound>se, like fluffy white hair.

短.meaning: A magic bowl of <part>beans</part> eats anything that touches it. You poke it with a <part>dart</part>: crunch, munch, and the dart comes back a stub no longer than your fingernail. The beans burp. Your dart is now very <kanji>short</kanji>.
短.on: It's small enough to roll through a mouse's <sound>tun</sound>nel in the skirting board.
短.kun: 'Give <sound>me</sound> a <sound>jee</sound>p and a <sound>ca</sound>rp,' burps the bowl, 'and I'll make them tiny too.'

令.meaning: A tiny general sits under a cocktail <part>umbrella</part> on <part>one</part> plank above the kitchen, pointing a <part>pizza wedge</part> like a baton. 'Cheese to the left! Olives, march!' The toppings obey. Nobody argues with his <kanji>orders</kanji>.
令.on: A <sound>ray</sound> flaps up out of the sink and salutes him with its fin.

完.meaning: A carpenter builds a whole house balanced on one <part>sawhorse</part>. When she nails on the last tile of the <part>roof</part>, nothing creaks, tilts or wobbles, not even when a goose lands on top. Every joint is <kanji>perfect</kanji>.
完.on: She tucks a pink <sound>car</sound>nation into the chimney to celebrate.

判.meaning: A cake-contest judge stabs a <part>dagger</part> into each entry and lifts out <part>half</part>. Hollow? Out. Raw? Out. The last one is chocolate all the way through, and she bangs her spoon like a gavel to give her <kanji>judgement</kanji>.
判.on: The winning cake turns out to be soaked in <sound>hon</sound>ey too.
判.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' gasps the crowd, and even a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond nods: understood.

裁.meaning: A palace guard is told to make the queen a dress. With no scissors, he swings his <part>halberd</part> at a roll of silk: swish, swish. Out falls a perfect <part>garment</part>, buttons and all. He quits guarding and becomes the royal <kanji>tailor</kanji>.
裁.on: His first customer pays him with a jug of apple <sound>ci</sound>der.
裁.kun: He slices the last loose thread and celebrates with a <sound>ta</sound>co.

弱.meaning: A kitten wants to shoot the cube of <part>ice</part> out of its milk bowl. It hauls on a big <part>bow</part> with both paws, then with its teeth, and the string barely moves. The arrow plops into the milk, and the ice cube bobs on, unharmed. The kitten's pull is hopelessly <kanji>weak</kanji>.
弱.on: Worn out, it flops into a bubbling <sound>jacu</sound>zzi to soak its sore paws.
弱.kun: '<sound>Yo</sound>gurt?' asks its mum. '<sound>Wah</sound>, my paws are too tired to lift a spoon!'

専.meaning: A farmer owns <part>ten</part> clubs but only ever uses one <part>golf club</part>. He plays the whole course through his <part>rice field</part>, chipping balls from paddy to paddy without splashing a drop. Muddy golf is his <kanji>specialty</kanji>.
専.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try stands by the last hole to stop the ducks stealing the balls.
専.kun: Afterwards he cleans his boots with a <sound>mop</sound> while his <sound>pa</sound> cheers from the bank.

修.meaning: A <part>fan seller</part> with long white <part>whiskers</part> makes his apprentice fold one paper fan a day, perfectly, for ten years. No breaks, no sweets, no grumbling. In the end the boy can fold one blindfolded in the dark. That's <kanji>discipline</kanji>.
修.on: Then he must balance each fan on the tip of a giant <sound>shoe</sound>.
修.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>,' sighs the master, handing him a thick <sound>sa</sound>ga to study next.

件.meaning: A <part>cow</part> wanders into a lawyer's office and hangs her bell on the <part>coat hook</part>. She's come about the missing hay. The lawyer opens a fat folder and licks her pencil: this is a serious <kanji>affair</kanji>.
件.on: The main suspect is the dog in the <sound>ken</sound>nel next door.
件.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the office clock and points at the <sound>dun</sound>geon key in the dog's mouth.

撃.meaning: A <part>maiden</part> in a flowing gown sees a toy <part>car</part> zoom straight at her cat. She raises one <part>hand</part>, chops the bonnet, and the car flips three times into the flowerbed. She can <kanji>beat</kanji> anything on wheels.
撃.on: A <sound>gec</sound>ko on the garden wall claps its sticky feet.
撃.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>ps,' she says, dusting off her hand and tossing the car into the bin.

射.meaning: A golfer with a huge <part>pot belly</part> can't see the ball past his tummy, so he props the <part>golf club</part> on top of it like a cannon and fires the ball off his belly button. It whistles into the hole from a mile away. Nobody else can <kanji>shoot</kanji> like that.
射.on: Next he fires a <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock the same way, feathers first.
射.kun: It knocks an <sound>ee</sound>l clean out of the water hazard.

証.meaning: A parrot in court gives a <part>speech</part>, repeating word for word what the burglar said on the night. Every word is <part>correct</part>, down to the burp at the end. The judge bangs her gavel: the parrot is the best <kanji>evidence</kanji>.
証.on: The trial turns into a <sound>show</sound>, with the parrot taking bows.
証.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasps a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the court fish tank, ducking behind a tiny <sound>shi</sound>eld.

船.meaning: A little rowing <part>boat</part> drinks a whole bottle of growing tonic through a <part>funnel</part>. Overnight it stretches, sprouts decks, cabins and a smoking chimney, and blasts its horn at the harbour. That dinghy is now a huge <kanji>ship</kanji>.
船.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try now marches up and down its deck day and night.
船.kun: The captain naps on a <sound>fu</sound>ton below deck with a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t over his face.

管.meaning: A <part>bureaucrat</part> wants water in his office, so he fills out forty forms, waits a year, and gets one hollow stick of <part>bamboo</part> poked through his window. A trickle runs down it into his teacup. At last, his very own <kanji>pipe</kanji>.
管.on: He pops a pink <sound>car</sound>nation into the end as a little vase.
管.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the far end of the pipe: 'Ta-<sound>da</sound>!'

余.meaning: Under a big beach <part>umbrella</part>, a gull keeps dropping fish onto a little stone <part>altar</part> in the sand, an offering for the sun. Ten fish, twenty, a hundred, until the altar tips over and they all slide back out to sea. Even the sun thinks that's <kanji>too much</kanji>.
余.on: The next day he brings just one small pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt instead.
余.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, <sound>ma</sound>ma,' sighs his chick, 'all the leftovers are for me!'

逃.meaning: A fortune-teller cracks open a shell and reads a terrible <part>portent</part>: 'Tomorrow, the taxman visits.' That night he greases the <part>ramp</part> to his front door with butter. The taxman steps on it and slides all the way back to the street, while the fortune-teller climbs out the back window. A perfect <kanji>escape</kanji>.
逃.on: Climbing out, he scrapes his big <sound>toe</sound> on the window frame but doesn't stop.
逃.kun: He bangs his <sound>knee</sound> on the garden fence and keeps on running.
